text:
maria: Quick runtime update — rolled out KV prefix caching + updated batching heuristic to hosted API canary (5%). Early numbers look good: median latency for long context (>=1024 tokens) down ~35%, p95 down ~27%, cost per token down ~18% on average. :tada:

sam: Nice! Which models and regions are in the canary?

maria: Canary targets: small/medium open models (redwood-base-v1, rw-lite-1b) in us-west1 and eu-west1. Dedicated/private unchanged for now. We enabled prefix_cache=true and adjusted batch_window from 15ms -> 8ms for short requests; increased max_batch_size floor for wide requests. Config snippet:

maria: ```
runtime_config:
  prefix_cache: true
  batch_window_ms: 8
  batching_strategy: dynamic
  max_batch_size: 256
```

kevin: Do we have memory or KV eviction regressions? Any uptick in OOMs?

maria: No OOMs in canary. Hit rate for prefix cache ~68% on trace workloads; average KV size reduced by ~22% vs naive caching. We saw a small increase in CPU usage on scheduler nodes (~6%) but GPU utilization improved due to better batching packing.

anika: Love to see the cost numbers. Is the 18% cost reduction measured on token billing or infra spend?

maria: Infra spend on hosted inference (GPU hours + egress) measured across canary traffic. Token billing for customers unaffected. We estimate pass-through savings to customers for public models via lower per-request compute multiplier.

deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout prefix-cache-canary -> 5% traffic at 2026-03-21T10:00Z

maria: Rollout plan: 5% -> 25% after 2h if no regressions -> 50% after 6h -> 100% after 24h. Watch p99 latency, error rate, cost-per-token, and model quality metrics. Dashboard: <https://internal.redwood/dashboards/runtime/prefix-cache-canary>

sam: I'll add alerts on p99+error spikes and numeric quality regression >1% on our eval set.

kevin: Can we toggle per-customer? Some enterprise customers might want opt-out.

maria: Yes, new flag in model route config: "prefix_cache: auto|on|off". Default is auto for hosted; Dedicated customers can opt to off via console or API. Example route patch command:

maria: ```
curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood/v1/routes/rt-123 \
  -d '{"prefix_cache":"off"}' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN'
```

anika: Heads up: we should post to #announcements and update docs about the new default.

maria: Will do. I'll open a tiny docs PR and an announcement post after 100% rollout. Thanks team — major props to @kevin and @anika for the scheduler tweaks :heart:

ops-bot: Summary saved: runtime/prefix-cache-canary 1765238400 -> p95 -27% median -35% cost -18% hit_rate 68% cpu_sched +6% gpu_util +12%

kevin: Anyone seen any model quality drift in canary traffic? Quick scan looked fine but double-checking.

maria: No quality drift detected in our eval checks so far. If anyone spots odd completions, tag me and we'll roll back the route flag for that model.

sam: Great work. I'll coordinate with support to pre-answer customer inquiries.

maria: Closing notes: we'll keep metrics in the dashboard and run a deeper perf/trace review next week to extract further wins (KV compression, smarter eviction).
